scope: Texas college students and youth: SNAP student rules, campus food pantries, FAFSA/TASFA help, Texas Youth Helpline, foster youth (PAL, ETV, tuition waiver, Transition Centers)

records.name: SNAP Food Benefits for College Students (Student Eligibility Rules)
records.organization: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
records.description_en: SNAP gives money on a Lone Star Card to buy groceries. College students enrolled half-time or more can get SNAP if they meet at least one special student exemption.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Students ages 18-49 enrolled at least half-time must meet one exemption, such as working 20+ hours a week, having work-study, getting TANF, being unable to work, being in an approved job training program, or caring for a dependent child. Regular SNAP income and resource rules also apply.
documents_needed: Proof of student exemption (for example work-study award letter or pay stubs showing 20+ hours per week)
records.how_to_apply: Apply online at YourTexasBenefits.com, or call 2-1-1 (option 2) for help. Many campuses (such as UT Austin's UT Outpost) have navigators who help students apply.
records.notes: Texas Works Handbook B-410 lists 8 exemptions: unable to work; working avg 20+ hrs/week; work-study during school year; WIOA/Choices/SNAP E&T/TAA or similar program; on-the-job training; approved for TANF; caring for a dependent child (age conditions apply); single parent enrolled full-time caring for a child under 12. Student age range is 18 through 49. Phone and apply link confirmed on hhs.texas.gov/services/food/snap-food-benefits.

records.name: Texas Youth Helpline
records.organization: Texas Department of Family and Protective Services (DFPS)
records.description_en: A free, private helpline for kids, teens, and families in crisis. You can call, text, or chat 24/7 to talk, make a plan, and get referrals to low-cost help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For youth, parents, guardians, and families in Texas who are having problems or are in crisis, including runaway youth.
records.how_to_apply: Call or text 1-800-989-6884, or use the chat on the DFPS Youth Helpline website. You do not have to give your name.
records.notes: Confidential; not a reporting hotline and not tied to law enforcement. Offers free messaging for runaway youth to contact family and connects to Operation Home Free (free transportation home). Referral database of 2,000+ Texas services.

records.name: 2-1-1 Texas
records.organization: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
records.description_en: 2-1-1 Texas is a free helpline that connects you to local help like food, housing, bills, health care, and child care. You can call or chat online.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone in Texas, including college students, who needs help finding local services.
records.how_to_apply: Dial 2-1-1 or 1-877-541-7905, or chat at 211texas.org in English or Spanish.
records.notes: Also the helpline for SNAP/Medicaid application questions.

records.name: UT Outpost Food Pantry and Career Closet
records.organization: The University of Texas at Austin, Student Outreach & Support
records.description_en: A free campus food pantry and career closet. Students can get up to 20 pounds of food a month, toiletries, menstrual and parenting products, and two outfits per semester.
records.eligibility_summary_en: All currently enrolled UT Austin students.
records.how_to_apply: Visit during open hours at the Student Services Building. One food visit per week.
records.address: 100 W Dean Keeton St, Student Services Building (SSB) G1.406
records.hours: Food pantry (September): Tue-Thu 1-6 pm, Fri 1-5 pm, 1st and 3rd Saturdays 10 am-2 pm. Career Closet: Tue 2-4 pm, Wed 1-3 pm, Fri 1-4 pm.
records.notes: Email utoutpost@austin.utexas.edu. Hours change by month/semester; check the page. Satellite locations also exist.

records.name: UT Outpost SNAP Application Help (Site and Peer Navigators)
records.organization: The University of Texas at Austin, Student Outreach & Support
records.description_en: Trained UT staff and peer navigators help students check if they qualify for SNAP and fill out the application.
records.eligibility_summary_en: UT Austin students who want help applying for SNAP food benefits.
documents_needed: Documents listed on Texas HHS Form H1858 (for example ID and proof of income)
records.how_to_apply: Book a SNAP Advising Session online, or email or call Student Outreach & Support.
records.notes: Email studentlife@austin.utexas.edu.

records.name: UT Austin Student Emergency Fund
records.organization: The University of Texas at Austin, Student Outreach & Support
records.description_en: Gives money to students facing a sudden emergency, like medical bills, medicine, City of Austin utility bills, lost belongings after a fire, or safety needs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Currently enrolled UT Austin students with a documented recent, short-term emergency. Awards depend on available funds.
documents_needed: Proof of the emergency (for example medical bills, police report, employment notice)
records.how_to_apply: Submit the application through the Student Outreach & Support portal with your documents. Processing usually takes about 5 business days.
records.notes: Does NOT cover rent/housing, ongoing costs (car payments, subscriptions), technology, or tuition.

records.name: The 12th Can Food Pantry
records.organization: The 12th Can (Texas A&M University student organization)
records.description_en: A student-run food pantry at Texas A&M that gives out free prepackaged food bags on scheduled opening weeks.
records.eligibility_summary_en: All Texas A&M students, staff, and faculty in need.
records.how_to_apply: Sign up when sign-ups are posted (Fridays 3:00-3:30 pm before opening weeks), or walk in during open hours.
records.address: Mail Services Building, Office #119, 330 Agronomy Rd
records.hours: Opens on a periodic schedule (next opening Sept 23-25, 2026); check website for dates.
records.notes: Volunteer-run; email 12thcan.director@gmail.com is preferred. Reachable by bus Route #6, Vet School stop.

records.name: Texas A&M Student Assistance Services
records.organization: Texas A&M University, Division of Student Affairs
records.description_en: Helps Texas A&M students with referrals and connections to resources when they face personal, financial, or academic problems.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Texas A&M University students.
records.how_to_apply: Call or email Student Assistance Services. For emergency aid, also contact the Financial Aid office at (979) 847-1787.
records.notes: Confirmed via the 12th Can's on-campus resource list. Email studentlife@tamu.edu. Financial Aid office offers emergency aid based on need.

records.name: Cougar Cupboard
records.organization: University of Houston
records.description_en: A free campus food pantry where UH students can get up to 30 pounds of groceries each week, including fresh produce, grains, and proteins.
records.eligibility_summary_en: All enrolled University of Houston students.
records.how_to_apply: Visit during open hours (Tuesday is by appointment only). Check Instagram @uhcupbrd for added hours.
records.address: 4200 Martin Luther King Blvd, Room R101
records.hours: Fall 2026: Tue 2-5 pm (appointments only), Wed 2-6 pm, Fri 10 am-2 pm, first Saturday of month 10 am-12 pm.
records.notes: Email uhcupbrd@cougarnet.uh.edu. Partners with Houston Food Bank. Phone listed is UH main line.

records.name: Roadrunner Pantry
records.organization: The University of Texas at San Antonio
records.description_en: Free food pantry at UTSA's Main and Downtown campuses to help students get healthy food. Order-ahead pickup is available.
records.eligibility_summary_en: All UTSA students, staff, and faculty in need, with a valid UTSA ID.
records.how_to_apply: Visit a pantry location during open hours or order ahead online. For after-hours help, email the pantry.
records.address: Main Campus: Student Union 1.04.06; Downtown: Durango Building 1.306
records.hours: Main Campus: Tue-Thu and Sat 10 am-4 pm. Downtown: Mon-Thu 12-4 pm.
records.notes: Downtown pantry phone (210) 458-2267. Email roadrunnerpantry@utsa.edu. Student Affairs emergencies: (210) 458-4140.

records.name: UTSA Emergency Aid (Grants and Loans)
records.organization: The University of Texas at San Antonio, One Stop / Financial Aid
records.description_en: One-time emergency grants or short-term loans for UTSA students facing a sudden crisis like car repairs, eviction notice, childcare loss, theft, job loss, or medical emergency.
records.eligibility_summary_en: UTSA students with a documented emergency. Grants require a completed FAFSA and other aid used first; students without a FAFSA may get a loan repaid within the semester.
documents_needed: Documentation of the emergency (for example eviction notice, repair estimate, medical bill)
records.how_to_apply: Submit the online Emergency Aid Application. You can also request a Financial Aid Re-Evaluation with a One Stop counselor if your income changed.
records.notes: Grants are one-time and while funds last. Toll-free (800) 669-0919; email onestop@utsa.edu.

records.name: UNT Food Pantry (Diamond Eagle Student Resource Center)
records.organization: University of North Texas, Dean of Students
records.description_en: Free groceries for UNT students once a week, plus a free clothing closet and professional clothes. Part of the Diamond Eagle Student Resource Center.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Currently enrolled UNT students facing food insecurity. Limit one visit per week.
records.how_to_apply: Walk in during open hours with your student ID. If you cannot come during hours, email DESresources@unt.edu for an appointment.
records.hours: Aug 17-Dec 2026: Mon-Wed 10 am-5 pm, Thu closed, Fri 10 am-5 pm, Sat 10 am-3 pm, Sun closed.
records.notes: Recently relocated to 621 S. Welch St. Follows the university closure calendar.

records.name: UTEP Food Pantry
records.organization: The University of Texas at El Paso, Student Affairs
records.description_en: A free food pantry for UTEP students who do not have enough food. A mobile pantry also runs on some days.
records.eligibility_summary_en: UTEP students experiencing food insecurity.
records.how_to_apply: Visit Memorial Gym during open hours. Check Instagram @utepfoodpantry for special hours during breaks.
records.notes: Email foodpantry@utep.edu. Mobile Food Pantry (summer 2026): Mondays 8:30-11:30 am at Helen of Troy Softball Field parking lot SB 10 on Sun Bowl Dr. Wheelchair accessible.

records.name: UTRGV Student Food Pantry
records.organization: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
records.description_en: Free food for UTRGV students at the Brownsville and Edinburg campuses. Enroll once, order online, then pick up on distribution days.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Currently enrolled UTRGV students.
records.how_to_apply: Fill out a one-time enrollment form at your pantry location, submit an online food order, and pick it up on a distribution day.
records.hours: Spring 2026 distribution: Brownsville Mon 12-3 pm, Fri 1-4 pm; Edinburg Mon 1-4 pm, Fri 11:30 am-3 pm.
records.notes: Email foodpantry@utrgv.edu. Hours shown were posted for Spring 2026; confirm current semester hours.

records.name: Riverbat Bites Food Pantry
records.organization: Austin Community College
records.description_en: Free groceries, fresh food at some campuses, heated grab-and-go meals, and personal care items like diapers, wipes, and period products.
records.eligibility_summary_en: All currently enrolled ACC students, at all eleven campuses.
records.how_to_apply: Visit a campus pantry during open hours. Some campuses (like Elgin and Riverside) require a pre-order form; Highland offers appointments.
records.hours: Varies by campus (for example Highland Mon-Fri 8:30 am-7 pm; Round Rock Mon-Fri 9 am-7 pm, varies by day).
records.notes: Campus list includes Hays, Highland, Round Rock, Elgin, Riverside and others; counties listed reflect confirmed campus locations (Elgin is in Bastrop County, Hays campus in Hays County, Round Rock in Williamson County).

records.name: ACC C.A.R.E. Network (Basic Needs Support)
records.organization: Austin Community College
records.description_en: ACC coordinators help students with food, housing, child care, mental health counseling, emergency funds, and help applying for SNAP and Medicaid.
records.eligibility_summary_en: ACC students. Most students qualify; coordinators check eligibility for each program at your appointment.
records.how_to_apply: Take the Basic Needs Questionnaire at austincc.edu/studentneeds, or schedule an appointment in the Student Appointment Portal.
records.address: ACC Round Rock Campus, Building 2000, Room 2110, 4400 College Park Drive
records.notes: Address/phone shown are for the Round Rock C.A.R.E. Network Center. ACC also has 'Campus Champions' support for former foster youth (per DFPS college partnerships page).

records.name: Eagle Markets Campus Food Pantries
records.organization: Houston City College (HCC, formerly Houston Community College)
records.description_en: Free campus food pantries with groceries and, at many campuses, hygiene and household items. Central Campus offers up to 60 pounds per visit, twice a month.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Currently enrolled HCC students. Each location has monthly visit limits.
records.how_to_apply: Visit an Eagle Market during open hours at your campus. For other help, fill out HCC's Basic Need Questionnaire or email HCC Cares.
records.hours: Varies by campus: Central Mon-Fri 9 am-5 pm (varies); Coleman Mon-Wed 9 am-3:30 pm; Northline Mon-Fri 9:30 am-3:30 pm; Southeast Mon-Fri 8:30 am-4:30 pm; Spring Branch Mon-Fri 9:30 am-4 pm; West Loop Mon-Thu 9 am-2 pm.
records.notes: The college's website now uses the name Houston City College. HCC Cares email: HCC.Cares@hccs.edu. Phone is the main college number. HCC's resource page also covers emergency funds, housing, childcare, transportation and SNAP eligibility info.

records.name: TASFA (Texas Application for State Financial Aid)
records.organization: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
records.description_en: TASFA is a Texas financial aid form for students who cannot or do not file the FAFSA. It lets you apply for state grants and aid at Texas colleges.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Texas residents who cannot or choose not to file the FAFSA. Students who file the FAFSA should not also file TASFA.
records.how_to_apply: Applications open October 1 each year. Get the TASFA (English or Spanish) and submit it to your college's financial aid office.
records.notes: THECB stresses the FAFSA gives access to more aid (federal, state and school). State aid programs include TEXAS Grant (universities) and Texas Educational Opportunity Grant/TEOG (community and technical colleges). Phone is THECB main line; students should usually contact their school's financial aid office.

records.name: Texas College Work-Study Program
records.organization: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board (run by each college)
records.description_en: State-funded part-time jobs that help students pay for college, including tutoring and mentoring jobs. Work-study can also help students meet a SNAP student exemption.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Eligible students at Texas colleges with financial need, as set by state guidelines and the school.
records.how_to_apply: File the FAFSA or TASFA, then ask your college's financial aid office about work-study jobs.
records.notes: Per Texas Works Handbook B-410, participating in work-study during the regular school year is a SNAP student exemption.

records.name: State College Tuition and Fee Waiver (Foster Care Exemption)
records.organization: Texas Department of Family and Protective Services / Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
records.description_en: Free tuition and fees at Texas public colleges and universities for current and former foster youth and youth adopted from DFPS care.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Youth who were in DFPS conservatorship on key dates (such as the day before turning 18, high school graduation, or adoption date), plus certain youth who returned to a parent. Must enroll before the age limit; youth adopted with an Adoption Assistance Agreement have no age limit.
records.how_to_apply: Get admitted to a Texas public college, then ask your regional PAL staff or Adoption Assistance specialist for Form 1810 and give it to your school. Request a new Form 1810 for each school you attend.
records.notes: AGE LIMIT CONFLICT: the DFPS page says you must enroll before your 27th birthday; the THECB Foster Care Exemption Fact Sheet says before age 25. Confirm with DFPS/school. Per THECB: no financial need test, Texas residency not required, GPA/excess-hours rules do not remove it, and it can be used for graduate study once eligible. Selective Service registration (or exemption) required.

records.name: Education and Training Voucher (ETV) Program
records.organization: Texas DFPS (administered by BCFS Health and Human Services)
records.description_en: Up to $5,000 a year for college or job training costs such as rent, utilities, books, computers, childcare, transportation, and tuition.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Current or former foster youth ages 16-23, including youth who aged out, were adopted from foster care after 16, or were in Permanency Care Assistance after 16. Must be enrolled at least 6 credit hours and keep satisfactory academic progress.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online at texasetv.com/apply, or call the ETV hotline for help. Your ETV Coordinator can help with school requirements.
records.notes: Maximum 5 years of funding; amount depends on cost of attendance and other aid. Administrative office: BCFS HHS, 4346 NW Loop 410, San Antonio, TX 78229.

records.name: Freshman and Sophomore Success Scholarship
records.organization: Texas Department of Family and Protective Services
records.description_en: A scholarship of $1,000 per semester (up to $2,000 for two semesters) for young adults who were in foster care and attend a Texas public college.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Young adults formerly in DFPS foster care attending a Texas state-funded community college, university, or technical college. Sophomores must have received the award both semesters as freshmen.
records.how_to_apply: Apply by August 1 (fall) or November 1 (spring) before each semester, using the application on the DFPS education resources page.
records.notes: Same page lists the C. Ed Davis PAL Scholarship ($1,000/year) for former foster youth in law-related majors. Texas colleges must help full-time former foster youth find housing during academic breaks.

records.name: Preparation for Adult Living (PAL)
records.organization: Texas Department of Family and Protective Services
records.description_en: PAL teaches foster youth life skills like money, housing, jobs, and health. It also offers a transitional living allowance and help paying room and board after leaving care.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Youth 16 and older in foster care likely to stay until 18 (some regions serve 14+), with services through age 21. Room and board aftercare is for ages 18-21 who aged out and are in school, work, or job training.
records.how_to_apply: Contact your caseworker or regional PAL staff (see the DFPS PAL staff list).
records.notes: Transitional Living Allowance: up to $1,000 ($500/month) after completing life-skills training and being employed, job-seeking, or in school. Aftercare Room & Board: up to $500/month, $3,000 lifetime cap, ages 18-21. Services depend on funding.

records.name: Extended Foster Care
records.organization: Texas Department of Family and Protective Services
records.description_en: Lets young adults who turn 18 in foster care stay in a placement with DFPS support until age 21 while they finish school, go to college, or work.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Young adults who turned 18 in DFPS care and are in high school/GED, in college, in an employment program, working 80+ hours a month, or unable to do these due to a documented medical condition.
records.how_to_apply: Contact regional PAL staff for pre-screening, then sign a Voluntary Extended Foster Care Agreement and start a qualifying activity within 30 days.
records.notes: Depends on an available placement. Youth who left care may be able to return. Pamphlets in English and Spanish.

records.name: DFPS Youth Housing Program
records.organization: Texas Department of Family and Protective Services
records.description_en: Helps young adults leaving foster care find housing, including Foster Youth to Independence (FYI) vouchers, Housing Choice Vouchers, and supervised independent living.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Young adults ages 18-24 with foster care involvement.
records.how_to_apply: Contact your regional youth housing liaison or email the DFPS housing program.
records.notes: Email CPSHousingProgram@dfps.texas.gov. A step-by-step housing guide is available on the page.

records.name: Medicaid for Transitioning and Former Foster Care Youth
records.organization: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
records.description_en: Free health coverage for young adults who were in Texas foster care. It covers doctor visits, prescriptions, hospital care, dental, vision, and rides to appointments.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Former Foster Care Youth: ages 18-25, in Texas foster care on 18th birthday or older and got Medicaid when aging out; no income limit. Transitioning Foster Care Youth: ages 18-20, in care through 18th birthday, income limits apply, no other insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online at YourTexasBenefits.com or call 2-1-1.
records.notes: DFPS also references the Former Foster Care in Higher Education (FFCHE) Medicaid program (Texas Works Handbook Part F) for former foster youth in college.

records.name: College Foster Care Liaisons
records.organization: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board (liaisons at each college)
records.description_en: Every Texas public college has at least one foster care liaison who helps students from foster care with enrollment, the tuition waiver, and campus and community resources.
records.eligibility_summary_en: College students who have experience in foster care.
records.how_to_apply: Look up your school's liaison in the THECB Foster Care Liaisons list, or ask your college's financial aid or student services office.
records.notes: Required by House Bill 3748. Campus programs listed by DFPS include ACC Campus Champions, Texas State FACES ($1,000 annual scholarship), Texas A&M College Station PAL staff contact, and SHSU FORWARD.

records.name: HAY Center (Houston Alumni and Youth Center)
records.organization: The HAY Center / Harris County
records.description_en: A one-stop Transition Center for current and former foster youth offering job help, education support, PAL classes, independent living help, and referrals.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Current and former foster youth; DFPS Transition Centers also serve homeless and other at-risk youth.
records.how_to_apply: Call or visit the center during business hours.
records.notes: DFPS lists (832) 927-7001; the HAY Center website lists 832-927-7000 or 832-927-0016. Hours from haycenter.org. Service area assumed Harris County (host county); confirm.

records.description_en: LifeWorks helps young people facing homelessness with housing, a drop-in center, counseling, education, and job services. It is also a DFPS Transition Center for foster youth.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Youth and young adults facing homelessness and current/former foster youth. Emergency shelter is for youth 17 and younger; adults 18+ are referred to other shelters.
records.how_to_apply: Call LifeWorks or visit the center.
records.notes: DFPS Transition Center phones: (512) 851-6434 / (800) 414-5457. LifeWorks main line (512) 735-2400, email LWinfo@lifeworksaustin.org. Service area assumed Travis/Central Texas; confirm.
